title: Russian cruiser Moskva sinks in the Black Sea
body:
The Moskva, flagship of Russia's Black Sea Fleet, sank in the Black Sea east of Snake Island on 14 April 2022. It was the largest Russian warship lost in wartime since the Second World War. On 13 April Odesa regional governor Maksym Marchenko said Ukrainian forces had hit the ship with two R-360 Neptune anti-ship missiles, causing serious damage.

Hours after the Ukrainian claim, the Russian Ministry of Defence said a fire had detonated ammunition and seriously damaged the ship, without mentioning a missile strike. On 14 April the ministry said the fire was contained and the ship was being towed to port, and later that day it said the ship had sunk during the tow in stormy weather. Pentagon spokesman John Kirby said on 14 April that the Ukrainian account was "certainly plausible", and on 15 April a senior U.S. official said the ship had been hit by two Neptune missiles. On 5 May a U.S. official said the United States had provided intelligence but that the decision to strike was Ukraine's alone.

Crew figures are disputed. On 22 April Russia stated that 396 crew had been rescued, one killed and 27 missing. The same day Ukraine's Oleksiy Danilov claimed the crew numbered 510 with only 58 rescued. Ukraine claimed about 452 killed, a figure that is unverified. A Sevastopol court declared 17 missing sailors dead on 4 November 2022.
